rules.title: PowerShell Execution of Script from NETLOGON Share

detection_logic.summary: Detects Sysmon process creation of PowerShell executing a script named simulated_wiper.ps1 from a NETLOGON UNC path.
detection_logic.sigma_yaml:
title: PowerShell Execution of Script from NETLOGON Share
id: 64fb8d77-7e1c-4fba-9bda-23794b4c5b8e
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
  selection_commandline:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '\\netlogon\\simulated_wiper.ps1'
      - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
  condition: selection_image and selection_commandline
falsepositives:
  - Authorized administrative or test automation executing a similarly named script from a NETLOGON share
level: high

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: Sysmon Event ID 1 contains data.process_image ending in powershell.exe and data.command_line invoking \\purplelab.local\netlogon\simulated_wiper.ps1 with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: Baseline Sysmon process creation shows hostname.exe and does not contain a PowerShell command line referencing a NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 path.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: Expected to match the Sysmon process creation whose data.command_line invokes the NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 script.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: Expected to produce no matches because the supplied baseline process creations do not reference NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 or ExecutionPolicy Bypass.

limitations: Only detects the observed script name and NETLOGON execution path pattern.
Requires process creation telemetry with Image and CommandLine fields.
Does not detect execution if PowerShell logging is absent and the command line omits the selected path or execution-policy terms.

deployment_target.description: Portable Sigma artifact; not actively deployed in the MVP

rules.title: PowerShell NETLOGON Script Execution Correlated with WiperTest File Removal

detection_logic.summary: Correlates PowerShell process creation invoking simulated_wiper.ps1 from NETLOGON with PowerShell telemetry showing Remove-Item activity against C:\WiperTest on the same host within five minutes.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The process_creation record has data.process_image C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe and data.command_line containing \\purplelab.local\netlogon\simulated_wiper.ps1.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The powershell record has data.script_text containing Remove-Item commands for files under C:\WiperTest.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: Baseline process creation is hostname.exe and its data.command_line does not contain a NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 path.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: Baseline PowerShell script text records hostname invocation and does not contain Remove-Item or C:\WiperTest.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: Expected to correlate the PowerShell process creation invoking the NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 path with subsequent PowerShell Remove-Item activity targeting C:\WiperTest on the same host.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: Expected to produce no matches because the supplied baseline lacks both a NETLOGON simulated_wiper.ps1 process invocation and PowerShell Remove-Item activity against C:\WiperTest.

limitations: Correlation is limited to records sharing an identical host value within 300 seconds.
The process stage depends on Sysmon process creation telemetry containing data.process_image and data.command_line.
The PowerShell stage depends on script or module logging retaining data.script_text with both Remove-Item and the target directory.
Legitimate automation using the same script name and target directory can generate alerts.

deployment_target.description: Windows machine running the Project Janus Python scripts
